subsystems.name: Print head array
subsystems.role: jets microscopic droplets of liquid photopolymer, one material at a time, across the build width.

subsystems.name: Material supply
subsystems.role: stores and delivers several different resins plus a dissolvable support material.

subsystems.name: Voxel data pipeline
subsystems.role: turns a solid CAD model into a grid of voxels, each stamped with a material or blend.

subsystems.name: Curing and levelling
subsystems.role: solidifies each deposited layer and keeps the surface flat for the next pass.

subsystems.name: Motion stage
subsystems.role: sweeps the head (or the platform) with micron-level accuracy so droplets land where intended.
parts: Z-stage that lowers the build tray

subsystems.name: Post-processing
subsystems.role: removes support, completes cure and finishes the part.

buildSteps.title: Model in voxels
buildSteps.detail: CAD geometry is voxelised — divided into millions of tiny cubes — and each voxel is assigned a material, a blend, or left empty.

buildSteps.title: Define material transitions
buildSteps.detail: Interfaces between materials are set as hard boundaries or graded mixtures, so stiffness can change gradually across a part.

buildSteps.title: Load materials
buildSteps.detail: Cartridges of the chosen photopolymers and a support resin are fitted and primed through the print heads.

buildSteps.title: Generate droplet maps
buildSteps.detail: Software slices the voxel grid into layers and converts each layer into a pattern of which nozzle fires where.

buildSteps.title: Print layer by layer
buildSteps.detail: The head array scans across the tray, jetting droplets of the selected materials side by side; a UV lamp cures the layer immediately behind the head.

buildSteps.title: Level and repeat
buildSteps.detail: A roller flattens the layer to an exact thickness, the build tray drops by one layer height, and the cycle repeats thousands of times.

buildSteps.title: Remove support
buildSteps.detail: The part is lifted out and the support material is dissolved or blasted away, leaving overhangs and internal channels intact.

buildSteps.title: Finish and verify
buildSteps.detail: A final UV cure hardens the part; dimensional checks and mechanical tests confirm the material map came out as designed.

prerequisites.tech: Inkjet print heads with reliable micron-scale droplets
prerequisites.why: the voxel resolution is limited by how small and repeatable a jetted droplet can be.

prerequisites.tech: Photopolymer resins that cure fast and bond to each other
prerequisites.why: adjacent voxels of different chemistry must cure together without delaminating.
internal voids and overhangs need support that can be removed without damaging the part.
conventional CAD treats a part as one material; assigning millions of voxels needs new toolchains and huge files.
running many reactive resins through one head risks clogging and mixing.

pathway.milestone: commercial inkjet photopolymer machines that print a handful of materials in one build
pathway.unlocks: prototypes with rigid and rubber-like regions, printed in a single pass.

pathway.milestone: research platforms pushing toward ten or more materials at voxel resolution
pathway.unlocks: parts whose stiffness, colour, conductivity or transparency vary point by point.

pathway.milestone: functionally graded components with no glued joints
pathway.unlocks: lighter parts for aerospace and medical implants where a hard surface meets a flexible core.

pathway.milestone: printing integrated devices — conductive, insulating and structural voxels in one object
pathway.unlocks: sensors, soft robots and custom prosthetics made in a single build.
